newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN CLINCH 1-1 DRAW AT VFB STUTTGART.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN CLINCH 1-1 DRAW AT VFB STUTTGART.

text.p: Bayern Munich won an important psychological battle in the German league title race on Sunday with a 1-1 draw at VfB Stuttgart, the most impressive team in the Bundesliga in the first half of the season.
Stuttgart needed an 80th-minute goal from Dutch captain Frank Verlaat to save the match after Bayern took an early lead on a seventh-minute penalty by German international midfielder Mario Basler.
After a largely bad-tempered south German derby, the home side had to play the last nine minutes with 10 men after midfielder Gerhard Poschner was sent off for seemingly complaining at the referee.
Bayern lost the top spot in the Bundesliga to Bayer Leverkusen but only goal difference separates the two teams before next weekend's final round of matches ahead of the winter break.
Stuttgart slipped down one place to third, two points behind the leading duo and just ahead of reigning champions Borussia Dortmund on goal difference.

Stuttgart's former Bayern defender Thomas Berthold was the most unfortunate player in the top-of-the-table clash which was played in front of a capacity 53,000 crowd on a freezing cold night in southern Germany.
The 1990 World Cup-winning defender almost put VfB ahead in the fifth minute when his header hit the post after a brilliant dribble and cross from the right from Brazilian striker Giovane Elber.

But just two minutes later the often controversial defender got his side into trouble, handling the ball in the area under pressure from Bayern's Italian striker Ruggiero Rizzitelli. Basler slotted the penalty perfectly into the left-hand corner.
Stuttgart, who until this season have failed to make an impact in the Bundesliga since they last won the title in 1992, took the game to the Bavarians.
Often they lacked composure and seemed too fired up. But their second-half pressure was finally rewarded when Verlaat fired in a cross from the right from close range.
Bayern striker Juergen Klinsmann, returning to the ground where he made his name in Germany with Stuttgart, had a disappointing match and was substituted in the second half.
